Draft 1. One major (29:11 auxiliador, the known adjútor objection), one minor (29:13 the passive). «A tradução conserva, nos demais versículos, o conteúdo latino e suas particularidades, sem substituí-las por leituras do hebraico.» Passed 'à minha custa', 'vós, seus santos', 'há ira na sua indignação', 'À tarde se demorará o pranto', 'Para sempre não serei abalado', 'destes vigor ao meu esplendor', 'lamento … júbilo', 'pano de saco'.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: adjútor is the one who helps; 'auxílio' puts the help for the helper → 'auxiliador'
outcomes.reason: Held (D19, D24): the row's one word, as at 9:10, 17:3b, 18:15b, 118:114; 'se fez o meu auxílio' is the natural predicate; no reader misheard it.

outcomes.remark: minor: compúngar is passive; the pronominal form does not keep the voice → 'e eu não seja compungido'

note: Draft 1. Four verses; best 29:3, worst 29:13. «Algumas inversões, uma rima de futuros e “compunja” ainda deixam ouvir o trabalho da tradução.» Two taken (29:13 in the Latinist's form), two refused with options.

outcomes.remark: subject after the long future is literary → 'O pranto se demorará à tarde'
outcomes.reason: The adverbs head both cola, the Latin's antithesis (ad vésperum … ad matutínum); his order makes a chiasm.

outcomes.remark: 'para sempre não' sounds transposed → 'Jamais serei abalado'
outcomes.reason: D23; 14:5b's build, which keeps the negation's scope; the second stylist to ask — evidence on the formula row.

outcomes.remark: 'compunja' needs deciphering, suggests remorse → 'e eu não seja ferido'
outcomes.reason: Taken in the Latinist's form, 'não seja compungido' (the Latin's word and voice; the participle is current); 'ferido' is an option.

note: Draft 1. 20 items, 2 unknown words (pano de saco, compunja). Wrong first hearings: 29:4 'inferno' as the hell of the damned (the inférnus row, D22 — for Gustavo), 29:10 'corrupção' as moral corruption (the corrúptio row's second place so heard). Heard rightly: 'à minha custa' (at my expense), 'vós, seus santos', 'há ira … vida na sua vontade', 29:6b (weeping lasts the evening), 'Para sempre não serei abalado' (not shaken), 'Desviastes de mim a vossa face', 'o pó' (the dead body), 'pano de saco' as coarse cloth worn (its mourning sense may be missed — not explained, as the Latin); 'a minha glória' left unidentified, as the Latin.

outcomes.remark: 'inferno' heard as the place of damnation first
outcomes.reason: The inférnus row, open for Gustavo (D22); evidence added.
Kept: the row's word and 15:10's (= Acts 2:27); 'decomposição' added as an option; evidence to the row.

outcomes.remark: 'pano de saco' unknown; mourning sense may be missed
outcomes.reason: Heard as coarse cloth worn — the Latin's image; its meaning is not explained (D2). 'o meu saco' would be a bag, or worse.

outcomes.remark: 'se demorará' second reading 'will be slow to come'; 'a alegria' may take the same verb
outcomes.reason: Heard first rightly; the verb is the glossary's (24:13).
